claims.claim: HTML is a markup language that browsers use to structure web pages, and it consists of elements that wrap or mark up content.
A common HTML element has an opening tag, content, and a closing tag; the closing tag includes a slash before the element name.
Properly nested elements close the inner element before the outer element, while overlapping tags require browser error recovery and can produce unexpected results.
Void elements cannot contain HTML content and have no separate closing tag; `br` is an example.
Attributes provide additional information about elements; a typical attribute uses a name, equals sign, and quoted value, and `class` can identify an element for CSS or JavaScript targeting.
Global attributes are attributes that may be specified on all HTML elements, whereas other attributes are element-specific.
